description: Dog must catch the 3:25 train! Learn the minute hand's lap of fives, read times to five minutes, and don't fall for the Sneaky Hour Hand at 7:50.

youtube.title: Telling Time to 5 Minutes! Catch the 3:25 Train | Grade 2 Math | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Dog's train to Grandma's leaves at 3:25, but Robo can't read the minute hand! Watch the minute hand run a lap of fives (5, 10, 15... 60) and learn why the 1 means 5 minutes.
Read 10:15, 2:40, 6:05 and 3:25, spot the Sneaky Hour Hand at 7:50, and help Dog reach every stop on time.
Try at home: make a paper-plate clock and read the kitchen clock at breakfast.

do.text: Five-Minute Clock Race
Robo! The train to Grandma's leaves at three twenty-five!
Let me look at the big clock. The long hand is on the 1.
So it's three... one? I don't know what that means!
Then we'd better learn the minute hand. Fast.
A clock has two hands, and each has its own job.
The short red hand is the hour hand.
hour hand
It shows the hour. It's just past 3.
The long blue hand is the minute hand.
minute hand
It shows how many minutes past the hour.
Remember from grade one? When the long hand is on 12...
it's o'clock! Four o'clock.
o'clock
And when the long hand is on 6, it's half past.
When I say short hand, you say hours!
Short hand?
Hours! Long hand?
Minutes! Great.
Fun fact: hands turn this way. We call it clockwise!
clockwise
Now the minute hand runs a lap of fives. Count with me!
But why does the 1 mean 5? The number says 1.
Great question! There are 60 minutes in one hour.
But a clock has only 12 numbers.
So 60 minutes are shared by 12 numbers. 5 each!
12 times 5 is 60. One whole lap is one hour.
60 minutes
Let's count the fives again, all the way round!
So at the start, the long hand was on 1. That's 5 minutes!
From three oh five to three twenty-five,
count the jumps: 5, 10, 15, 20.
Twenty minutes until my train! Phew.
Robo, read the hour first, then count the fives.
Let's read some times. Short hand first.
The short hand is just past 10.
Long hand on 3. Count by fives!
5, 10, 15. It's ten fifteen!
Next one.
The long hand is on 8. How many minutes?
The hour hand is between 2 and 3, so it's two forty.
Here's a tricky one.
Just past 6, and the long hand is on 1.
Six oh five! We write a zero before the 5.
And now the train time!
Short hand past 3. Long hand on 5. That's...?
Three twenty-five! Dog's train time!
See? The hour hand is a bit less than halfway to 4.
Now beware of the Sneaky Hour Hand!
Easy! The short hand is on 8. It's eight fifty!
Look closely, Robo. The hour hand is almost at 8.
Almost, but not yet. So it's still 7. Seven fifty!
Oh! The hour hand is sneaky. I read it too fast.
But why is it so close to 8 if it's still 7?
Let's watch. The hour hand walks slowly,
while the long hand runs.
Here's eight o'clock. Now watch one whole hour.
The long hand went all the way round.
The short hand only moved from 8 to 9!
Fun fact:
the hour hand needs a whole hour to reach the next number.
So at fifty minutes, it's nearly there. Sneaky, but slow.
Make a long arm and sweep it round. Chant with me!
Tick, tock, five more minutes,
round we go, the long hand knows!
Tick, tock, five more minutes,
round we go, the long hand knows!
I have stops before the train.
Can you help me with the times?
Dog leaves home at two forty. Where does the long hand go?
On the 8! Two forty.
Bye, house! Off I go.
Next stop, the market at two fifty-five.
Long hand on 11. The hour hand is almost at 3,
but it's still 2!
Apples for Grandma!
Then the park at three ten.
Long hand on 2. 5, 10. Three ten!
Check the hour hand too. Just past 3. Good.
Sing while Dog walks! Tick, tock, five more minutes!
Then the station at three twenty.
Long hand on 4. Three twenty!
I made it to the station! Five minutes to spare.
From three twenty to three twenty-five is one jump of five.
Challenge! Four clocks, three seconds each. Ready?
Three seconds each. Hour first, then count by fives.
Four thirty-five! The long hand is on 7.
Eleven ten! The long hand is on 2.
Nine forty-five! The long hand is on 9.
Twelve fifty-five! The hour hand is almost at 1,
but it's still 12.
You didn't fall for the sneaky hour hand. Nice.
And here comes the train. What time is it now?
Three twenty-five! Right on time!
Quiz time! The long hand points at 9. How many minutes?
45! 9 jumps of 5.
The short hand is just past 4,
the long hand is on 2. What time?
Four ten!
Why does the 1 on a clock mean 5 minutes?
60 minutes shared by 12 numbers is 5 each.
Last one. Is this eight fifty or seven fifty?
Seven fifty! The hour hand isn't at 8 yet.
All aboard! Dog rides to Grandma's.
Right on time.
Read a clock at home today, and count by fives. Bye!
